basic_info.name: FHIRPath libraries (HL7 fhirpath.js, beda-software fhirpath-py, nazrulworld fhirpath)
basic_info.description: FHIRPath is the HL7 expression language used across FHIR for constraints/invariants, profile logic, search-parameter definitions, SDC/CQL supplements and data extraction; these are the three main open-source implementations outside the Java reference engine. HL7/fhirpath.js is the de-facto JavaScript implementation - developed jointly by the U.S. National Library of Medicine (Lister Hill National Center for Biomedical Communications) and Health Samurai, then donated to HL7 and currently maintained by NLM; it ships on npm as fhirpath (current 5.2.0, package updated 2026-08-25; weekly downloads on the order of 30-50K) under a BSD-style NLM/LHNCBC license, and works in both Node.js and the browser with an ANTLR4-generated parser, FHIR model data for DSTU2/STU3/R4/R5/R6, async functions, terminology-service APIs, user-defined functions and a CLI. beda-software/fhirpath-py (PyPI: fhirpathpy) is the actively maintained Python implementation under MIT, with an ANTLR4 parser, prebuilt DSTU2/STU3/R4/R5 models, evaluate/compile APIs and user-defined functions, and it is currently at 2.2.x (2.2.0 Apr-2026, 2.2.1 Jun-2026, a further 2.2.x on 2026-08-01). nazrulworld/fhirpath is the stale Python alternative: its last PyPI release was 0.10.5 on 2020-12-17 (no release in roughly 5.7 years), Python 3.6-based, ORM/Elasticsearch-oriented, and its license is ambiguous - PyPI metadata declares GPLv3 while the GitHub repository banner shows Apache-2.0. The load-bearing fact for MediKiosk is that fhirpath.js and fhirpath-py are both lightweight, offline, CPU-only, permissively licensed expression engines that can run on the kiosk itself for targeted constraint checks and summary-section extraction, whereas they are not full profile validators - real NRCeS IG conformance still needs the ShapeDefinition/validator layer (Matchbox/HAPI/validator_cli).
basic_info.organization: HL7/fhirpath.js: created by the U.S. National Library of Medicine's Lister Hill National Center for Biomedical Communications (LHNCBC) and Health Samurai (niquola), donated to Health Level Seven International (HL7), currently maintained by NLM. beda-software/fhirpath-py: beda.software, an open-source health-IT engineering company (primary contributors ir4y, ruscoder, plus brianpos). nazrulworld/fhirpath: Md Nazrul Islam (individual maintainer, GitHub user nazrulworld).
basic_info.country: United States for fhirpath.js (NLM/NIH); beda.software is a distributed/remote open-source company (formerly associated with Armenia); nazrulworld is an individual maintainer. All are globally used, with no India-specific origin.
basic_info.status: Mixed. fhirpath.js: production, actively maintained (npm 5.2.0, package updated 2026-08-25; many releases across 2026). beda-software/fhirpath-py: production, actively maintained (2.2.0 through 2.2.x releases across 2026; GitHub 76 stars, 17 forks, 9 open issues). nazrulworld/fhirpath: dormant/stale - last PyPI release 0.10.5 on 2020-12-17, effectively unmaintained for nearly six years (GitHub still shows 34 stars, 7 forks, 414 commits, 6 open issues and 6 open pull requests).

technical_features.what_it_does: These libraries parse and evaluate FHIRPath expressions against FHIR resources/Bundles and return collections of values. In the Module C context FHIRPath is the language the ABDM/NRCeS IG itself uses to express constraints and invariants, so a FHIRPath engine is what you call to (a) evaluate targeted conformance assertions on an emitted bundle (e.g. 'must have exactly one Composition', 'each section has a title', 'identifier system is the ABHA namespace') and (b) extract summary sections and fields (e.g. pull all Observation/MedicationStatement/Condition entries out of a Document Bundle, walk Composition.section, read Patient identifiers) for building the physician-facing summary. fhirpath.js additionally supports async functions (resolve(), memberOf(), %terminologies.*), user-defined functions, a trace callback, precise decimal math, and precompilation for repeated use across many resources. fhirpath-py provides evaluate() and compile() plus prebuilt DSTU2/STU3/R4/R5 models and user-defined functions. Both are expression engines only - they do not perform StructureDefinition/profile validation, cardinality enforcement or terminology binding validation by themselves.
technical_features.architecture: fhirpath.js: an ANTLR4-generated core parser (grammar in parser/FHIRPath.g4) with an evaluator over a ResourceNode tree that adds FHIR type/path metadata, per-version model packages under fhir-context/{dstu2,stu3,r4,r5,r6} (choice-type support), separate CommonJS and self-contained ESM entry points, browser bundles (fhirpath.min.js plus optional fhirpath.r4.min.js), a CLI (bin/fhirpath) and a demo page. fhirpath-py: an ANTLR4-generated parser plus an evaluator, with models for DSTU2/STU3/R4/R5, an evaluate/compile API, a resource-node abstraction, and user-definable invocation tables; distributed as a small pure-Python package. nazrulworld/fhirpath: a larger ORM-like framework where FHIRPath is implemented alongside a FHIR Search engine and an FQL query builder, with pluggable providers/dialects (Elasticsearch, Plone, guillotina) and hard dependencies on fhir.resources/fhirspec.
technical_features.inputs: A FHIR resource or Bundle as a plain JSON object/array (JS object or Python dict), a FHIRPath expression string (or an object with base+expression for partial resources), optional environment variables (e.g. %resource, %questionnaire), an optional FHIR-version model object (for choice-type resolution), and evaluation options (async, terminologyUrl, fhirServerUrl, httpHeaders, signal, preciseMath, keepDecimalTypes, resolveInternalTypes, traceFn, userInvocationTable in fhirpath.js; model and userInvocationTable in fhirpath-py). nazrulworld's engine additionally consumes database/Elasticsearch connections and indexes.
technical_features.outputs: A collection (array) of matched values, optionally with internal FHIRPath types preserved; type information via fhirpath.types(); parsed AST (CLI); and - where terminology/fhir servers are configured - results of memberOf()/resolve()/memberOf lookups. Used in Module C it produces extracted field/section values and boolean/numeric results for conformance assertions; it does not itself produce a validated bundle or a clinical summary.
technical_features.standards_compliance: All three are implementations of the HL7 FHIRPath specification. fhirpath.js explicitly targets FHIRPath 2.0.0 while noting some behaviour still follows STU1; its README lists completed spec sections (3, 5.x, 6.x, 7, 8, 9) and supported additional functions (extension, hasValue, getValue, resolve, memberOf, comparable, htmlChecks) plus the FHIRPath Terminology Service APIs (%terminologies.expand/lookup/validateVS/validateCS/subsumes/translate), SDC supplements (sum/min/max/count/avg/ordinal/weight) and Type Factory APIs. It ships FHIR model context for DSTU2/STU3/R4/R5 and is being extended to R6. fhirpath-py ships models for DSTU2/STU3/R4/R5. These are language-compliance claims backed by test suites (the FHIRPath test suite and the official R4 examples), not NRCeS/ABDM profile compliance - neither library validates resources against the ndhm.in IG. The critical caveat for Module C: feature conformance and profile conformance are different layers; FHIRPath evaluates an expression, while StructureDefinition/cardinality/binding enforcement lives in the validator (HAPI/Matchbox/validator_cli).
technical_features.offline_capability: Both active libraries are fully offline-capable by default: they are local parsers/evaluators with the FHIR model data bundled in the package, and they require no network for ordinary path/filter/math/string evaluation. Network is only invoked for optional async features explicitly configured with terminologyUrl or fhirServerUrl (memberOf, resolve, %terminologies); in a disconnected kiosk those options are simply omitted. This makes them suitable for on-device use under MediKiosk's offline-first and India-residency constraints, provided terminology-dependent expressions are avoided or served by a local terminology server. nazrulworld's engine is `not a kiosk fit`: it assumes external engines/databases (Elasticsearch/Plone/guillotina).
technical_features.languages_supported: Not natural-language tools. FHIRPath string functions operate on arbitrary Unicode strings, so Hindi/Devanagari and code-mixed Hinglish values in FHIR fields can be matched, concatenated and compared using generic string functions (e.g. contains, startsWith, substring), but there is no tokenisation, transliteration, collation or bilingual rendering. [uncertain] No Indic-script-specific behaviour was documented for any of the three libraries.
technical_features.deployment_model: fhirpath.js: embeddable in any Node.js service and directly loadable in a web browser, so it can run on the kiosk UI (browser/Electron/Tauri) or a local Node service; no GPU, tiny footprint (npm unpacked size ~2.4 MB, 7 dependencies). fhirpath-py: a pure-Python package (>=3.10) embedded in a Python backend or edge service; no GPU. nazrulworld/fhirpath: a Python >=3.6 framework that expects external data stores/providers, so it is not a lightweight on-device component. All are CPU-only and fit comfortably within a ~4 GB kiosk budget when used as libraries.

performance_metrics.accuracy_or_quality_metrics: No accuracy/F1/ROUGE-style metrics apply - these are deterministic interpreters. The quality signal is spec conformance and test coverage: fhirpath.js runs the FHIRPath test suite plus Jest unit tests and Cypress browser tests and documents a detailed implementation-status matrix, and it explicitly reports its known deviations (e.g. parts of FHIRPath 2.0 not yet complete). fhirpath-py publishes codecov coverage and runs pytest on GitHub Actions. Neither publishes an aggregate conformance score. Determinism (same input -> same output) is the property that matters for Module C and is inherent to expression evaluation, which is why FHIRPath is attractive for reproducible, explainable conformance checks.
performance_metrics.latency: No official latency/throughput benchmarks. The structural cost driver in fhirpath.js is the optional preciseMath mode (decimal-safe arithmetic), which the README describes as a moderate performance cost versus native JavaScript math; the default is native math for speed. fhirpath-py's 2.0.1 (May 2026) release explicitly 'increase[d] performance of parsing'. Both offer a compile() API so an expression is parsed once and reused across many resources, which is the recommended pattern for batch validation or extraction. For kiosk-scale workloads (one bundle per patient, tens to hundreds of expressions) these costs are negligible.
performance_metrics.resource_requirements: Minimal. fhirpath.js is a JavaScript package (unpacked ~2.4 MB, 7 dependencies) that runs in Node.js or the browser with no GPU; fhirpath-py is a small pure-Python package requiring Python >= 3.10 with an ANTLR4-generated parser and no GPU. Both fit easily on a CPU/iGPU kiosk and can run in the same process as the kiosk application. nazrulworld/fhirpath requires Python >= 3.6 plus external provider infrastructure (e.g. Elasticsearch), which raises its footprint and operational complexity.
performance_metrics.scale_metrics: Adoption is concentrated in fhirpath.js and fhirpath-py. fhirpath.js: ~189 GitHub stars, 51 forks, 1,423 commits, 142 npm versions since first publish 2018-08-01, ~92 npm dependents, and weekly downloads reported in the range of roughly 30,000-50,000 (figures differed between npm snippets). fhirpath-py: 76 stars, 17 forks, 9 open issues, regular PyPI releases. nazrulworld/fhirpath: 34 stars, 7 forks, 414 commits, but no release since 2020. These are library-ecosystem metrics, not deployed-user volumes.
performance_metrics.evaluation_protocol: Quality is established by conformance test suites against the formal FHIRPath test suite and FHIR example resources, plus CI (Jest/Cypress for fhirpath.js; pytest + GitHub Actions + codecov for fhirpath-py). There is no benchmark comparison between the implementations, no peer-reviewed evaluation and no clinical-quality evaluation, and none is applicable - the relevant Module C verification is whether chosen expressions produce the expected results on known-good and known-bad ABDM bundles.

milestone_significance.relevance_to_module_c: FHIRPath is the mechanism Module C needs at two points. First, conformance checking: the NRCeS/ABDM IG expresses many of its requirements as FHIRPath constraints and invariants, so evaluating FHIRPath on an emitted OPConsultRecord/DocumentBundle is how you run targeted checks cheaply and offline - but note this is assertion-layer checking, not full profile validation, so it complements (does not replace) a Matchbox/HAPI/validator_cli pass against ndhm.in. Second, section extraction: Module C must turn a conversational-history bundle plus digitised documents into one structured summary, which means walking a Document Bundle's Composition.section entries and pulling Patient, Condition, Observation, MedicationStatement, Procedure and AllergyIntolerance resources into summary fields - exactly what FHIRPath path/filter/projection expressions do, with precompiled expressions for speed. The choice matters for MediKiosk's offline, CPU/iGPU and India-residency constraints: both fhirpath.js (browser/Node) and fhirpath-py (Python) are lightweight, permissively licensed, network-free expression engines that can run on the kiosk, whereas nazrulworld/fhirpath should not be used at all.
milestone_significance.what_to_adopt_or_reject: Adopt: (1) HL7/fhirpath.js if the kiosk pipeline or summary renderer is JavaScript/TypeScript, or beda-software/fhirpath-py if it is Python - both are active, permissively licensed (BSD-style and MIT respectively) and offline; (2) precompilation (compile() then reuse) for the handful of extraction and assertion expressions Module C runs per patient; (3) user-defined functions to expose application-specific helpers (e.g. an ABHA-identifier check or a bilingual normaliser) without forking the engine; (4) fhirpath.js's terminology-server option only where a local terminology server exists, and otherwise pure path/filter expressions; (5) FHIRPath as the expression language for a small, versioned, machine-readable 'Module C conformance rules' file so the assertion set is auditable alongside physician attestation. Reject or avoid: (1) nazrulworld/fhirpath - stale (last release 2020) and with a GPLv3/Apache-2.0 licence conflict, an unacceptable dependency risk; (2) treating FHIRPath results as full IG validation - cardinality, slicing, must-support and terminology bindings need the real validator; (3) any expression that requires memberOf()/expand()/resolve() at a disconnected kiosk without a local terminology server; (4) relying on fhirpath.js's in-progress FHIRPath 2.0 features without testing the specific functions used.
milestone_significance.limitations_and_risks: The main risk is category error: FHIRPath evaluates expressions but does not validate a resource against a StructureDefinition, so a green set of FHIRPath checks is not evidence of NRCeS conformance - only the validator layer (Matchbox/HAPI/validator_cli with the ndhm.in package) can assert that, and ABDM will reject malformed bundles regardless of FHIRPath results. fhirpath.js is not OSI-labelled ('Other/NOASSERTION' on GitHub) even though the LICENSE.md is BSD-based with a no-endorsement clause naming NLM/LHNCBC/NIH - permissive for commercial use but worth a legal read; it is also still working toward full FHIRPath 2.0. fhirpath-py is younger with a smaller contributor base. nazrulworld/fhirpath is the clearest liability: no release since 2020-12-17, Python 3.6-era, and a licence mismatch (PyPI says GPLv3, repo banner says Apache-2.0) that must be resolved before any use. Cross-implementation differences in model/choice-type handling and numeric/date semantics mean results can differ between engines, so Module C should pin one implementation and version and test it against the exact expressions it ships. Finally, none of these publishes benchmarks, so any performance claim at kiosk scale should be measured locally rather than assumed.
milestone_significance.differentiator_vs_medikiosk: These libraries are utilities, not competitors, and adopting an active, permissively licensed one strengthens MediKiosk: it enables deterministic, offline, on-device conformance assertions and summary-section extraction, reinforcing the offline-first, India-residency and NRCeS-conformant-emission differentiators and supporting the per-field provenance goal (each extracted field can carry the FHIRPath expression and source path that produced it). They erode nothing - they contain no elicitation, no summarisation, no document digitisation, no AYUSH/Prakriti logic and no physician attestation. The nuance is that FHIRPath is a commodity implementation layer; the defensibility stays in how Module C designs its extraction/assertion rules and resolves the AYUSH gap, not in the choice of expression engine.

business_info.license: fhirpath.js: a BSD-style licence, developed jointly by LHNCBC/NLM and Health Samurai with terms 'based on the BSD open-source license'; commercial and non-commercial redistribution allowed with attribution and a no-endorsement clause (NLM/LHNCBC/NIH names may not endorse derived products). GitHub's automated label is 'Other/NOASSERTION', so it is not OSI-badged despite the BSD wording. beda-software/fhirpath-py: MIT License, Copyright (c) 2020 beda.software - clean permissive terms. nazrulworld/fhirpath: licence conflict - PyPI metadata lists GNU GPLv3 while the GitHub repository banner shows Apache-2.0; this ambiguity must be resolved before use because GPLv3 would impose copyleft obligations on a kiosk product. [uncertain]
business_info.pricing: All three are free, open-source libraries with no fee, paid tier or commercial terms. fhirpath.js and fhirpath-py are published on npm and PyPI respectively; nothing is charged for use.
business_info.funding: fhirpath.js: funded/institutionally supported by the U.S. National Library of Medicine (NLM/NIH public funding) and originally co-developed with the commercial company Health Samurai, then donated to HL7; no venture funding applies. beda-software/fhirpath-py: developed by beda.software as part of its open-source health-IT portfolio (company-funded). nazrulworld/fhirpath: unfunded individual effort. [uncertain] No detailed financials were researched.
business_info.commercial_status: Open-source projects. fhirpath.js is effectively public-sector/standards-body funded (NLM into HL7); fhirpath-py is company-sponsored open source; nazrulworld/fhirpath is an unpaid individual project that is no longer maintained.

competition_ecosystem.competitors: Other FHIRPath implementations and engines: the Java reference engine inside org.hl7.fhir.core (used by HAPI FHIR, Matchbox, the IG Publisher and validator_cli), Firely's .NET FHIRPath engine (part of the Firely .NET SDK), FHIRPath Lab (web evaluation service, which ahdis integrated with), and various embedded engines in FHIR servers. Among Python options, fhirpath-py competes with the stale nazrulworld/fhirpath. The practical Module C choice is fhirpath.js (JS/TS stack) versus fhirpath-py (Python stack); the Java engine is relevant only if validation is done with Matchbox/HAPI, which uses FHIRPath internally for invariants.
competition_ecosystem.integrations: fhirpath.js is distributed via npm (CommonJS and ESM) and as browser bundles, with a CLI and demo page; it supports configuration of terminology servers (%terminologies APIs), FHIR servers for resolve(), HTTP headers/auth, AbortSignal cancellation, and user-defined function tables; it is used by NLM's LForms tooling. fhirpath-py is on PyPI, integrates with Python services and provides user-defined function tables and FHIR-version models. Both interoperate with FHIR data from any source. There is no ABDM/NRCeS-specific integration in any of them, and no HIP/HIU/PHR gateway coupling.
competition_ecosystem.ecosystem_notes: FHIRPath is a normative/spec-level part of FHIR, so the ecosystem pull is toward stable, standards-track engines, which favours the HL7-hosted fhirpath.js and the active fhirpath-py over the abandoned nazrulworld package. For MediKiosk the broader implication is that the expression-evaluation layer is a commodity: offline, standards-faithful, permissively licensed engines are freely available, so effort should go into the Module C rule set, extraction schema and the AYUSH/Prakriti gap rather than into building an expression engine. The main ecosystem risk is licence hygiene (fhirpath.js's non-OSI BSD-style label and nazrulworld's GPL/Apache conflict), which a government-facing project should clear early.

history.release_date: fhirpath.js: the npm package was first published 2018-08-01 and the GitHub repository was created for HL7 hosting on 2019-04-01 (development began earlier at NLM/Health Samurai before donation to HL7). fhirpath-py: GitHub repository created 2020-02-24; the PyPI package fhirpathpy's first listed release is 0.0.1 on 2022-07-01. nazrulworld/fhirpath: first PyPI release 0.1.0 on 2018-12-15, latest 0.10.5 on 2020-12-17.
history.key_milestones: fhirpath.js: development at NLM/Health Samurai, donation to HL7, and steady 1.x-3.x maturation; 2024-2026 saw accelerated releases (3.13.3 in Jun 2024, then the 4.x line through 2025 and 2026) with the addition of ESM packaging, FHIR model contexts for DSTU2/STU3/R4/R5, async functions, terminology-service APIs, Type Factory APIs, precise-math and decimal-preservation options, the CLI, and the start of R6 model support. fhirpath-py: initial releases in 2022-2023, 1.0.0 in Jan 2024, 2.0.0 in Mar 2025 (with datetime millisecond support and user-defined functions), and 2.2.x in 2026. nazrulworld/fhirpath: ORM/FQL/Elasticsearch-oriented releases through 2019-2020, then no published release after 0.10.5 (2020-12-17).
history.recent_changes_last_6_months: fhirpath.js shipped a dense sequence in the window: 4.9.0-4.9.3 (Feb-Mar 2026), 4.10.0 (2026-04-21) and 4.10.1 (2026-05-04), 4.11.0 (2026-05-29), then the major 5.0.0 (2026-07-13), 5.1.0 (2026-07-29), 5.1.1 (2026-08-05) and 5.2.0 (npm package updated 2026-08-25). 5.0.0 is the notable change: it preserves metadata-only ResourceNodes when resolveInternalTypes is false (a behaviour change for raw-result consumers, with a documented filter workaround), and the 5.x line added a self-contained bundled ESM entry point so bundlers like esbuild/Angular CLI stop warning about CommonJS, plus ongoing terminology-API and htmlChecks work. beda-software/fhirpath-py released 2.2.0 (2026-04-16), 2.2.1 (2026-06-10, fixing to_date/to_date_time conversion), and a further 2.2.x on 2026-08-01 adding a $this evaluation-context fix, a traceFn callback, a returnRawData option and ResourceNode propName/index properties (contributed by brianpos). nazrulworld/fhirpath had no releases or activity in the window. Net: choose fhirpath.js or fhirpath-py; both are current; nazrulworld is not.

market_positioning.target_users: FHIR software developers and health-IT engineers building validators, IG tooling, form engines (e.g. NLM LForms), questionnaire/SDC systems, CQL/clinical-logic tooling, data-mapping pipelines and EHR integrations - anyone who needs to evaluate FHIRPath in JavaScript/TypeScript or Python. Secondary users are standards implementers and test labs. Not an end-user product.
market_positioning.market_segment: FHIR tooling - expression-language engines / developer libraries in the interoperability layer. Not intake, ambient scribing, PHR, AYUSH software, diagnostics kiosk or benchmarking.
market_positioning.positioning_statement: fhirpath.js positions itself as 'FHIRPath implementation in JavaScript', hosted officially under the HL7 GitHub organisation, developed by NLM and Health Samurai, with the pitch that it works server-side in Node.js and in the browser, follows the FHIRPath specification (currently moving to 2.0.0), and offers async functions, terminology-server support, user-defined functions and a CLI. beda-software/fhirpath-py positions itself simply as 'FHIRPath implementation in Python', with an ANTLR4 parser, prebuilt FHIR-version models, and a small evaluate/compile API plus user-defined functions. nazrulworld/fhirpath pitched a broader ORM-like FHIRPath + FHIR Search + FQL framework with pluggable engines/providers, but that positioning is no longer maintained.
